Our funded deliverables install the selected customers’ source and receiving workflows: the analyst reviews the original material, acquires the complete agreed output, continues its editable business task and transfers the working installation to another maintainer.|
|**Nirium.** The maintained [SDK repository](https://github.com/nirium-protocol/nirium) provides TypeScript and Python clients, MCP and CLI interfaces, buyer-side x402 payment and `x402Serve()` seller middleware. Treasury and audit capabilities extend that platform.|Existing SDKs and facilitator integrations supply the payment foundation. Our package acceptance is the customer’s full source-to-result operation, including its application mappings, aggregate purchase state, interrupted delivery and installed response. Compatibility is assessed against each selected service’s actual scheme and terms.|
|**MPP Router and its Stellar agent wallet.** The [published wallet client](https://github.com/mpprouter/stellar-agent-wallet-skill) discovers services, pays x402 or MPP-gated calls with Stellar USDC and checks expected recipients and amounts. The [router workflow](https://www.mpprouter.dev/how-it-works) connects service discovery to a paid request.|Discovery and paid API access are established options. The proposed installation additionally defines what a complete customer job contains, retains every required result and source edition, and opens that output in the customer’s existing application. A later reporting period or source revision supplies a distinct useful purchase.|
|**Stellar Raven.** SDF’s [remote MCP service](https://raven.stellar.org/docs) combines searchable operations, executable service composition, official Stellar documentation and identified community information sources.|This supports developer research and integration. Our awarded deliverable is the operated merchant/buyer service, its customer data and its receiving maintainer. The original source and payment authority remain explicit throughout that installation.|


**Business value and adoption.** The first customer is an organization commissioning a repeatable information or application operation: for example, a complete filing comparison, reviewed laboratory delivery or recurring economic report. Its workorder names the commissioning payer, resource merchant, independent buyer and receiving engineer, with one agreed output and acceptance procedure. TokenJunkieLabs earns the fixed implementation fee and separately scoped care; the merchant retains its resource receipts. Selection favors a real reason for repeat use, an authorized source, a customer application that can receive the result and a maintainer who can operate the installation. The existing conversation records and delivery examples inform that selection.

**Technical improvement to be delivered.** The reusable product joins the original source, approved request and terms, native transfer, complete usable result and required fulfillment in one continuing customer operation. For a paginated dataset that includes its whole selected population; for a file or report it includes the complete bytes and the source edition used to produce them. An interrupted request reopens with its original financial and delivery state. Another authorized engineer receives the working configuration, decisions, history and customer files and completes the same task on the receiving host.

The six funded packages apply that architecture to the selected customers. T1 completes both source/application adaptations and a second operator’s handover. T2 operates the same useful service through two facilitators and completes the installed recovery cases. T3 establishes recurring mainnet use, restores the production state and completes independent maintenance. These are the proposed improvements reviewers can evaluate: useful customer output, repeat independent purchases, preserved operation when the payment provider changes and an installation another engineer can maintain.

**Open Track scope.** We selected Open Track for the merchant and buyer operating application and its reusable source-to-result workflow. It composes the existing x402 SDKs, payment services and facilitator catalogues. The funded improvement preserves source meaning and pagination, reviews exact requests and terms, acquires the complete result, receives it into the customer’s application or workbook, and reopens the service after interruption or on another authorized host. The six packages publish the adaptations required to operate that application across independently maintained services. Useful customer output, repeat purchases and successful receiving define the resulting ecosystem value. This application-level contribution and the business and technical comparison above explain the proposed [Open Track fit](https://stellar.gitbook.io/scf-handbook/scf-awards/build-award/open-track).

A retained comparison found 27 Vellar offers and two Periplo offers with no shared seller/route identity. The two-facilitator deliverable therefore includes actual registration and integration of the **same useful service** with both operators. Its completion must preserve the customer operation when payment infrastructure changes. Reusable integration, receiving and operating improvements return to the public source.

## Defined architecture and operating behavior

The system has six components: the merchant’s private source/release workspace; its public HTTP or MCP operation; the native Stellar SDK and facilitator; the buyer’s private approval and spending state; complete-result and delivery records; and merchant fulfillment/accounting. Node.js supplies merchant and buyer interfaces. Source adapters and receiving applications retain their own native data and operating semantics.

|Stage|Implemented behavior|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|Review and publish|The merchant selects a source edition or named live query, request schema, output, limits and resolved payment options. Review includes source rights, route, network, asset, recipient, amount and authorization lifetime. Source or terms changes become later reviewed states.|
|Connect the source|Adapters preserve types, missing and null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select authorized access. The output identifies its source edition.|

|Operate and hand over|The customer selects its release, HTTPS service, restricted administration and supervision. A receiving engineer can drain, restart, roll back and restore the installation with its operating history and complete customer files.|

## Why Stellar and what we contribute

Stellar supplies the settlement for the operation the buyer approved. Each approval binds the request to its network, asset, recipient and integer atomic amount. The native Stellar SDK and selected facilitator verify and settle that authorization. The application associates the returned settlement with the original request, complete output and merchant action. The buyer retains signing and aggregate spending authority; the merchant controls its resource and terms.

We compose the existing x402 Exact Stellar scheme, SDKs, token contracts and facilitators, including the selected provider’s actual payment requirements and optional discovery extension. The existing MPP Charge integration retains its own challenge and recovery model.

There are close alternatives. [ApiCharge](https://communityfund.stellar.org/project/apicharge-djv) combines service publication and consumption with Soroban settlement and signed agreements. [Nirium](https://github.com/nirium-protocol/nirium) provides Stellar payment SDKs, seller middleware, MCP and CLI interfaces. [MPP Router](https://www.mpprouter.dev/how-it-works) supplies service discovery and paid calls; [Stellar Raven](https://raven.stellar.org/docs) supplies ecosystem context and integration operations through MCP. Our application completes the customer’s continuing operation around payment: source review, complete paginated or file output, receiving into its business application, interrupted-operation recovery, and transfer of the working service to another maintainer.

We propose [Open Track](https://stellar.gitbook.io/scf-handbook/scf-awards/build-award/open-track) for this reusable merchant-and-buyer operating application. The funded contribution is the source-to-result and receiving workflow across independent services, with published implementation and deployment improvements. The retained catalogue comparison found 27 Vellar offers and two Periplo offers with no shared seller/route identity, so this package includes real same-service registration and compatibility. Repeat independent purchases and successfully operated customer installations measure the value to Stellar.

## Defined architecture and operating behavior

The architecture has six components: a private merchant source/release workspace; its public HTTP or MCP operation; the Stellar SDK and facilitator; private buyer approval and spending state; retained delivery records and complete output; and merchant fulfillment/accounting.

1. **Select and publish.** The merchant chooses an authorized source edition or named live query, schema, output and limits. Review resolves the route, network, asset, recipient, amount and authorization lifetime. Later source or terms changes become separately reviewed states.
2. **Connect the source.** Adapters preserve types, null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select access. The returned result identifies its source edition.
3. **Approve and pay.** The buyer retains the HTTP method or MCP tool, arguments, scope and payment option. The remote schema and full challenge, including authorization lifetime, must match before signing. For paid MCP, the endpoint, tool and arguments remain separate from the payment resource; the official MCP SDK carries payment and settlement metadata. Per-payment limits and the existing reservation/budget owner govern aggregate spending.
4. **Settle and receive.** The facilitator verifies and settles the native authorization. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the network, asset, parties and atomic amount. The application retains the complete output, merchant notification and receiving acknowledgment. A multi-request acquisition keeps its aggregate cost and unfinished coverage. Saved prepaid calls retain their selected pass; a replacement links to its predecessor and acquired results remain available.
5. **Use and account.** The receiving application opens every page and file needed for the task. Merchant pricing connects the selected tariff and saved uniform quote to an actual usage period, counting basis and supplier-cost basis. A reviewed price change carries its measured source into the customer quotation and original invoice or service records.
6. **Recover and hand over.** Server confirmation, observed transfer, output and fulfillment retain separate states. An uncertain signed response is reconciled through its original dispatch. The receiving engineer restores configuration, history and customer files, supplies authorized secret references and continues the same operation.

Node.js supplies the merchant, buyer, browser, CLI, typed-client and MCP interfaces. Source adapters and receiving applications retain their native semantics. The maintained implementation also uses Python and SQLite for typed data and saved queries, and PHP for WordPress/WooCommerce integration. New contracts are outside this six-package request; the product uses existing SDKs and token contracts.

## Project and requested outcome

TokenJunkieLabs is building open-source, self-hostable software that lets a merchant sell a useful API, dataset or agent operation on Stellar and lets the buyer receive the complete result in its existing application.

We request **$38,000 for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from award acceptance**. ## Why Stellar and what we contribute

Stellar supplies the settlement for the operation the buyer approved. Each approval binds the request to its network, asset, recipient and integer atomic amount. The native Stellar SDK and selected facilitator verify and settle that authorization. The application associates the returned settlement with the original request, complete output and merchant action. The buyer retains signing and aggregate spending authority; the merchant controls its resource and terms.

We compose the existing x402 Exact Stellar scheme, SDKs, token contracts and facilitators, including the selected provider’s actual payment requirements and optional discovery extension. The existing MPP Charge integration retains its own challenge and recovery model.

There are close alternatives. [ApiCharge](https://communityfund.stellar.org/project/apicharge-djv) combines service publication and consumption with Soroban settlement and signed agreements. [Nirium](https://github.com/nirium-protocol/nirium) provides Stellar payment SDKs, seller middleware, MCP and CLI interfaces. [MPP Router](https://www.mpprouter.dev/how-it-works) supplies service discovery and paid calls; [Stellar Raven](https://raven.stellar.org/docs) supplies ecosystem context and integration operations through MCP. Our application completes the customer’s continuing operation around payment: source review, complete paginated or file output, receiving into its business application, interrupted-operation recovery, and transfer of the working service to another maintainer.

We propose [Open Track](https://stellar.gitbook.io/scf-handbook/scf-awards/build-award/open-track) for this reusable merchant-and-buyer operating application. The funded contribution is the source-to-result and receiving workflow across independent services, with published implementation and deployment improvements. The same-service, two-facilitator deliverable includes the required registration and payment-policy integration. The retained catalogue comparison found 27 Vellar offers and two Periplo offers with no shared seller/route identity, so this package includes real same-service registration and compatibility. Repeat independent purchases and successfully operated customer installations measure the value to Stellar.

## Defined architecture and operating behavior

The architecture has six components: a private merchant source/release workspace; its public HTTP or MCP operation; the Stellar SDK and facilitator; private buyer approval and spending state; retained delivery records and complete output; and merchant fulfillment/accounting.

**Select and publish.** The merchant chooses an authorized source edition or named live query, schema, output and limits. Review resolves the route, network, asset, recipient, amount and authorization lifetime. Later source or terms changes become separately reviewed states.

**Connect the source.** Adapters preserve types, null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select access. The returned result identifies its source edition.

**Approve and pay.** The buyer retains the HTTP method or MCP tool, arguments, scope and payment option. The remote schema and full challenge, including authorization lifetime, must match before signing. For paid MCP, the endpoint, tool and arguments remain separate from the payment resource; the official MCP SDK carries payment and settlement metadata. Per-payment limits and the existing reservation/budget owner govern aggregate spending.

**Settle and receive.** The facilitator verifies and settles the native authorization. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the network, asset, parties and atomic amount. The application retains the complete output, merchant notification and receiving acknowledgment. A multi-request acquisition keeps its aggregate cost and unfinished coverage. Saved prepaid calls retain their selected pass; a replacement links to its predecessor and acquired results remain available.

**Use and account.** The receiving application opens every page and file needed for the task. Merchant pricing connects the selected tariff and saved uniform quote to an actual usage period, counting basis and supplier-cost basis. A reviewed price change carries its measured source into the customer quotation and original invoice or service records.

**Recover and hand over.** Server confirmation, observed transfer, output and fulfillment retain separate states. An uncertain signed response is reconciled through its original dispatch. The receiving engineer restores configuration, history and customer files, supplies authorized secret references and continues the same operation.

Node.js supplies the merchant, buyer, browser, CLI, typed-client and MCP interfaces. Source adapters and receiving applications retain their native semantics. The maintained implementation also uses Python and SQLite for typed data and saved queries, and PHP for WordPress/WooCommerce integration. New contracts are outside this six-package request; the product uses existing SDKs and token contracts.

**Select and publish.** The merchant chooses an authorized source edition or named live query, schema, output and limits. Review resolves the route, network, asset, recipient, amount and authorization lifetime. Later source or terms changes become separately reviewed states.

**Connect the source.** Adapters preserve types, null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select access. The returned result identifies its source edition.

**Approve and pay.** The buyer retains the HTTP method or MCP tool, arguments, scope and payment option. The remote schema and full challenge, including authorization lifetime, must match before signing. For paid MCP, the endpoint, tool and arguments remain separate from the payment resource; the official MCP SDK carries payment and settlement metadata. Per-payment limits and the existing reservation/budget owner govern aggregate spending.

**Settle and receive.** The facilitator verifies and settles the native authorization. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the network, asset, parties and atomic amount. The application retains the complete output, merchant notification and receiving acknowledgment. A multi-request acquisition keeps its aggregate cost and unfinished coverage. Saved prepaid calls retain their selected pass; a replacement links to its predecessor and acquired results remain available.

**Use and account.** The receiving application opens every page and file needed for the task. Merchant pricing connects the selected tariff and saved uniform quote to an actual usage period, counting basis and supplier-cost basis. A reviewed price change carries its measured source into the customer quotation and original invoice or service records.

**Recover and hand over.** Server confirmation, observed transfer, output and fulfillment retain separate states. An uncertain signed response is reconciled through its original dispatch. The receiving engineer restores configuration, history and customer files, supplies authorized secret references and continues the same operation.

Node.js supplies the merchant, buyer, browser, CLI, typed-client and MCP interfaces. Source adapters and receiving applications retain their native semantics. The maintained implementation also uses Python and SQLite for typed data and saved queries, and PHP for WordPress/WooCommerce integration. The original merchant accounting exercise completed invoice issue, credit, receipt allocation, Xero-format receiving, correction and cold reopening. The tariff example completed selection, native repricing, backup and receiving: a 1,250-request graduated tariff totaled $14.25 and produced the saved $0.0114 uniform quote.

The installed product also delivers named reports, spreadsheets and supporting files through Jobs and Resource library, retaining the original request, payment and completed attempt. These are the proposed improvements reviewers can evaluate: useful customer output, repeat independent purchases, preserved operation when the payment provider changes and an installation another engineer can maintain.

The six packages publish the adaptations required to operate that application across independently maintained services. Useful customer output, repeat purchases and successful receiving define the resulting ecosystem value. |Stage|Implemented behavior|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|Review and publish|The merchant selects a source edition or named live query, request schema, output, limits and resolved payment options. Review includes source rights, route, network, asset, recipient, amount and authorization lifetime. Source or terms changes become later reviewed states.|
|Connect the source|Adapters preserve types, missing and null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select authorized access. The output identifies its source edition.|
|Approve and purchase|The buyer retains the endpoint, method or MCP tool, arguments, selected terms and scope. The remote schema and challenge must match before signing. Per-payment limits and the application’s existing reservation/budget owner govern spending.|
|Settle and deliver|The facilitator verifies and settles the native authorization. The application retains the server outcome, complete output and durable merchant notification. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the transaction’s network, asset, parties and atomic amount.|
|Use and continue|The receiving application opens all pages and files required by the task. A parent acquisition retains its priced requests and unfinished coverage. Earlier acquired output remains available when a later source edition changes.|
|Operate and hand over|The customer selects its release, HTTPS service, restricted administration and supervision. A receiving engineer can drain, restart, roll back and restore the installation with its operating history and complete customer files.|


**Recurring editorial data products.** The delivered WordPress merchant workspace turns a later source edition into a reviewable customer product. The operator saves an approved baseline as a refresh plan, continues the original native capture, inspects the complete source and projected changes, and approves the exact candidate before issuing its successor through the existing publisher. The same browser, CLI and agent interfaces preserve earlier acquired editions, original request identities and unfinished decisions when another engineer receives the workspace. This supplies a concrete recurring-use workflow for the selected customer installations. [Merged implementation and complete operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/1135e64cca2da5948c2d3e2c78119094d88f41d2/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/wordpress/REFRESH.md).

For paid MCP, the HTTP endpoint, tool and arguments are retained separately from the payment resource. An unsigned call obtains the challenge. Its full payment option, including authorization timeout, must match the saved quote before the buyer retains dispatch state and sends the signed call. The official MCP SDK carries payment and settlement metadata. HTTP operations use the native HTTP transport.

Recovery keeps server confirmation, independently observed transfer, complete output, receiver acknowledgment and fulfillment separately visible. An uncertain signed response stays attached to its original dispatch for reconciliation. Reopening an acquired result uses saved work; unfinished delivery continues from its original intent. A changed request or new purchase receives a new review.

Browser, terminal, typed clients and MCP operate the same retained workspaces. Customer exports include configuration selection, history and all referenced files. The receiving host supplies current authorized secret references. Buyer accounting also carries reviewed expense and credit allocations into connected QuickBooks and Xero accounts, with review of changed charts, affected mappings and journal lines before application.

The merchant's pricing workspace connects those operations to its customer offer. It retains the approved tariff and saved uniform quote, selects the actual usage period and counting basis, and compares their values with the recorded supplier-cost basis. The operator enters the monthly quantity for a proposed change, reviews the resulting native price, and carries the measured source into an ordinary customer quotation revision. The original pricing, scenario and Commercial workspaces retain the same requests and history. [Merged usage, pricing and quotation workflow](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/318).

The merchant financial workspace carries that paid operation into its original settlement accounting and customer records. An invoice can issue reviewed Stellar wallet terms; native receiving verifies the returned transfer and applies its original customer receipt. Issued service invoices retain exact amounts and billing identity; actual receipts, dated allocations and credits determine the balance. Reviewed installment plans distribute that balance across due dates and preserve every customer edition. The Xero handover maps issued invoices and credits to the receiving organisation's original templates, retains returned document IDs and exact amounts, and continues corrections through the same package family. Native network, asset and atomic amount remain attached to the original settlement; commercial valuations retain their explicit basis. Each installation records its source edition, merchant/buyer authority, network and facilitator, protected records, reviewed thresholds, notification destinations and named primary/backup responders.

The plan connects the actual threats to observations and permitted responses: changed offers or approvals; incorrect financial or output attribution; unauthorized authority or access; interrupted delivery; lost monitoring; and restoration of the wrong generation. A confirmed integrity contradiction opens an incident. Age, rate and capacity thresholds use the installation’s reviewed values.

Acceptance operates two cases against the deployed service: an interrupted settled purchase and a merchant-delivery failure. Their records retain the actual notification and acknowledgment, financial and delivery outcomes, response and recovery times, material remediation or residual findings, and the receiving engineer’s same-case reopening after drain/restart. An uncertain payment is reconciled through its original intent. A coverage gap remains visible until observation resumes.

A completed purchase joins a distinct approved intent, an independently observed native transfer and complete useful output. Native transactions are counted once within each network. The cohort counts distinct accountable operator IDs whose reviewed deployment identifies an independent operator or customer, its buyer or merchant role, source basis, required network and operating or handed-over state. An operator’s agents and wallets share that identity; they do not create additional independent buyers. These are source-supported operator declarations, not automatic verification of corporate independence. Team-operated development purchases do not qualify. A returning buyer completes distinct intent groups on at least two UTC days. Reopening an acquired result or resuming its download continues the original purchase. Facilitators are also deduplicated by accountable operator for the same useful operation. [Original cohort operator guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/fcea2b04a19d9c14bbd337124ecdc83f5e36425c/stellar/scf_2026/sf47_budget_model/workspace/OPERATIONS-COHORT.md).

Cohort reporting includes completed/attempted purchases, complete/started parent datasets or files, returning buyers, accepted handovers and partial, unresolved, canceled and refunded outcomes. **Business value and adoption.** The first customer is an organization commissioning a repeatable information or application operation: for example, a complete filing comparison, reviewed laboratory delivery or recurring economic report. Its workorder names the commissioning payer, resource merchant, independent buyer and receiving engineer, with one agreed output and acceptance procedure. TokenJunkieLabs earns the fixed implementation fee and separately scoped care; the merchant retains its resource receipts. Selection favors a real reason for repeat use, an authorized source, a customer application that can receive the result and a maintainer who can operate the installation. The existing conversation records and delivery examples inform that selection.

**Technical improvement to be delivered.** The reusable product joins the original source, approved request and terms, native transfer, complete usable result and required fulfillment in one continuing customer operation. For a paginated dataset that includes its whole selected population; for a file or report it includes the complete bytes and the source edition used to produce them. An interrupted request reopens with its original financial and delivery state. Another authorized engineer receives the working configuration, decisions, history and customer files and completes the same task on the receiving host.

The six funded packages apply that architecture to the selected customers. T1 completes both source/application adaptations and a second operator’s handover. T2 operates the same useful service through two facilitators and completes the installed recovery cases. T3 establishes recurring mainnet use, restores the production state and completes independent maintenance. These are the proposed improvements reviewers can evaluate: useful customer output, repeat independent purchases, preserved operation when the payment provider changes and an installation another engineer can maintain.

**Open Track scope.** We selected Open Track for the merchant and buyer operating application and its reusable source-to-result workflow. It composes the existing x402 SDKs, payment services and facilitator catalogues. The funded improvement preserves source meaning and pagination, reviews exact requests and terms, acquires the complete result, receives it into the customer’s application or workbook, and reopens the service after interruption or on another authorized host. The six packages publish the adaptations required to operate that application across independently maintained services. Useful customer output, repeat purchases and successful receiving define the resulting ecosystem value. This application-level contribution and the business and technical comparison above explain the proposed [Open Track fit](https://stellar.gitbook.io/scf-handbook/scf-awards/build-award/open-track).

A retained comparison found 27 Vellar offers and two Periplo offers with no shared seller/route identity. The two-facilitator deliverable therefore includes actual registration and integration of the **same useful service** with both operators. **Business value and adoption.** The first customer is an organization commissioning a repeatable information or application operation: for example, a complete filing comparison, reviewed laboratory delivery or recurring economic report. Its workorder names the commissioning payer, resource merchant, independent buyer and receiving engineer, with one agreed output and acceptance procedure. Selection favors a real reason for repeat use, an authorized source, a customer application that can receive the result and a maintainer who can operate the installation. **Technical improvement to be delivered.** The reusable product joins the original source, approved request and terms, native transfer, complete usable result and required fulfillment in one continuing customer operation. For a paginated dataset that includes its whole selected population; for a file or report it includes the complete bytes and the source edition used to produce them. An interrupted request reopens with its original financial and delivery state. Another authorized engineer receives the working configuration, decisions, history and customer files and completes the same task on the receiving host.

Acceptance operates two cases against the deployed service. The existing MPP Charge workbench retains its own challenge, authorization and recovery model. The implementation uses existing SDKs and token contracts.

**Business value and adoption.** The first customer is an organization commissioning a repeatable information or application operation: for example, a complete filing comparison, reviewed laboratory delivery or recurring economic report. Its workorder names the commissioning payer, resource merchant, independent buyer and receiving engineer, with one agreed output and acceptance procedure. TokenJunkieLabs earns the fixed implementation fee and separately scoped care; the merchant retains its resource receipts. Selection favors a real reason for repeat use, an authorized source, a customer application that can receive the result and a maintainer who can operate the installation. The existing conversation records and delivery examples inform that selection.

**Technical improvement to be delivered.** The reusable product joins the original source, approved request and terms, native transfer, complete usable result and required fulfillment in one continuing customer operation. For a paginated dataset that includes its whole selected population; for a file or report it includes the complete bytes and the source edition used to produce them. An interrupted request reopens with its original financial and delivery state. Another authorized engineer receives the working configuration, decisions, history and customer files and completes the same task on the receiving host.

The six funded packages apply that architecture to the selected customers. T1 completes both source/application adaptations and a second operator’s handover. T2 operates the same useful service through two facilitators and completes the installed recovery cases. T3 establishes recurring mainnet use, restores the production state and completes independent maintenance. These are the proposed improvements reviewers can evaluate: useful customer output, repeat independent purchases, preserved operation when the payment provider changes and an installation another engineer can maintain.

**Open Track scope.** We selected Open Track for the merchant and buyer operating application and its reusable source-to-result workflow. It composes the existing x402 SDKs, payment services and facilitator catalogues. The funded improvement preserves source meaning and pagination, reviews exact requests and terms, acquires the complete result, receives it into the customer’s application or workbook, and reopens the service after interruption or on another authorized host. The six packages publish the adaptations required to operate that application across independently maintained services. Useful customer output, repeat purchases and successful receiving define the resulting ecosystem value. This application-level contribution and the business and technical comparison above explain the proposed [Open Track fit](https://stellar.gitbook.io/scf-handbook/scf-awards/build-award/open-track).

|Stage|Implemented behavior|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|Review and publish|The merchant selects a source edition or named live query, request schema, output, limits and resolved payment options. Review includes source rights, route, network, asset, recipient, amount and authorization lifetime. Source or terms changes become later reviewed states.|
|Connect the source|Adapters preserve types, missing and null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select authorized access. The output identifies its source edition.|
|Approve and purchase|The buyer retains the endpoint, method or MCP tool, arguments, selected terms and scope. The remote schema and challenge must match before signing. Per-payment limits and the application’s existing reservation/budget owner govern spending.|
|Settle and deliver|The facilitator verifies and settles the native authorization. The application retains the server outcome, complete output and durable merchant notification. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the transaction’s network, asset, parties and atomic amount.|
|Use and continue|The receiving application opens all pages and files required by the task. A parent acquisition retains its priced requests and unfinished coverage. Earlier acquired output remains available when a later source edition changes.|
|Operate and hand over|The customer selects its release, HTTPS service, restricted administration and supervision. A receiving engineer can drain, restart, roll back and restore the installation with its operating history and complete customer files.|


**Recurring editorial data products.** The delivered WordPress merchant workspace turns a later source edition into a reviewable customer product. The operator saves an approved baseline as a refresh plan, continues the original native capture, inspects the complete source and projected changes, and approves the exact candidate before issuing its successor through the existing publisher. The same browser, CLI and agent interfaces preserve earlier acquired editions, original request identities and unfinished decisions when another engineer receives the workspace. This supplies a concrete recurring-use workflow for the selected customer installations. [Merged implementation and complete operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/1135e64cca2da5948c2d3e2c78119094d88f41d2/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/wordpress/REFRESH.md).

For paid MCP, the HTTP endpoint, tool and arguments are retained separately from the payment resource. An unsigned call obtains the challenge. Its full payment option, including authorization timeout, must match the saved quote before the buyer retains dispatch state and sends the signed call. The official MCP SDK carries payment and settlement metadata. HTTP operations use the native HTTP transport.

Each installation retains a compatibility profile identifying its complete source release, installed buyer and signer SDK versions, facilitator registration, network, supported asset, authorization flow and fee policy. The original approval and signer checks must accept that profile before dispatch. A provider or network change receives an explicit new selection and preserves earlier purchases and source editions. T2 receives the same useful service through both testnet facilitators; T3 receives both mainnet merchant installations under their actual selected profiles.

Recovery keeps server confirmation, independently observed transfer, complete output, receiver acknowledgment and fulfillment separately visible. An uncertain signed response stays attached to its original dispatch for reconciliation. Reopening an acquired result uses saved work; unfinished delivery continues from its original intent. A changed request or new purchase receives a new review.

Browser, terminal, typed clients and MCP operate the same retained workspaces. Customer exports include configuration selection, history and all referenced files. The receiving host supplies current authorized secret references. Buyer accounting also carries reviewed expense and credit allocations into connected QuickBooks and Xero accounts, with review of changed charts, affected mappings and journal lines before application.

The merchant's pricing workspace connects those operations to its customer offer. It retains the approved tariff and saved uniform quote, selects the actual usage period and counting basis, and compares their values with the recorded supplier-cost basis. The operator enters the monthly quantity for a proposed change, reviews the resulting native price, and carries the measured source into an ordinary customer quotation revision. The original pricing, scenario and Commercial workspaces retain the same requests and history. [Merged usage, pricing and quotation workflow](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/318).

The merchant financial workspace carries that paid operation into its original settlement accounting and customer records. An invoice can issue reviewed Stellar wallet terms; native receiving verifies the returned transfer and applies its original customer receipt. Issued service invoices retain exact amounts and billing identity; actual receipts, dated allocations and credits determine the balance. Reviewed installment plans distribute that balance across due dates and preserve every customer edition. The Xero handover maps issued invoices and credits to the receiving organisation's original templates, retains returned document IDs and exact amounts, and continues corrections through the same package family. Sponsored settlement lets the buyer pay in the selected supported token while the facilitator covers the transaction fee. Existing Stellar wallets, token contracts and payment services provide this native foundation.

The merchant and buyer workspaces retain the HTTP endpoint and method or MCP tool and arguments, request-body identity, selected source or query, and accepted payment option. We compose existing ecosystem infrastructure. The x402 Exact Stellar scheme and facilitator supply payment verification and settlement. Vellar’s optional discovery extension publishes eligible settled resources to its catalogue. OpenZeppelin, Veridex and Periplo supply relevant payment infrastructure, while Rumble Fish is developing facilitator, discovery and SDK capabilities. The existing MPP Charge workbench retains its own challenge, authorization and recovery model. The implementation uses existing SDKs and token contracts.

**Business value and adoption.** The first customer is an organization commissioning a repeatable information or application operation: for example, a complete filing comparison, reviewed laboratory delivery or recurring economic report. Its workorder names the commissioning payer, resource merchant, independent buyer and receiving engineer, with one agreed output and acceptance procedure. TokenJunkieLabs earns the fixed implementation fee and separately scoped care; the merchant retains its resource receipts. Selection favors a real reason for repeat use, an authorized source, a customer application that can receive the result and a maintainer who can operate the installation. The existing conversation records and delivery examples inform that selection.

**Technical improvement to be delivered.** The reusable product joins the original source, approved request and terms, native transfer, complete usable result and required fulfillment in one continuing customer operation. For a paginated dataset that includes its whole selected population; for a file or report it includes the complete bytes and the source edition used to produce them. An interrupted request reopens with its original financial and delivery state. Another authorized engineer receives the working configuration, decisions, history and customer files and completes the same task on the receiving host.

The six funded packages apply that architecture to the selected customers. T1 completes both source/application adaptations and a second operator’s handover. T2 operates the same useful service through two facilitators and completes the installed recovery cases. T3 establishes recurring mainnet use, restores the production state and completes independent maintenance. These are the proposed improvements reviewers can evaluate: useful customer output, repeat independent purchases, preserved operation when the payment provider changes and an installation another engineer can maintain.

**Open Track scope.** We selected Open Track for the merchant and buyer operating application and its reusable source-to-result workflow. It composes the existing x402 SDKs, payment services and facilitator catalogues. The funded improvement preserves source meaning and pagination, reviews exact requests and terms, acquires the complete result, receives it into the customer’s application or workbook, and reopens the service after interruption or on another authorized host. The six packages publish the adaptations required to operate that application across independently maintained services. Each installation records its source edition, merchant/buyer authority, network and facilitator, protected records, reviewed thresholds, notification destinations and named primary/backup responders.

The plan connects the actual threats to observations and permitted responses: changed offers or approvals; incorrect financial or output attribution; unauthorized authority or access; interrupted delivery; lost monitoring; and restoration of the wrong generation. A confirmed integrity contradiction opens an incident. Age, rate and capacity thresholds use the installation’s reviewed values.

Acceptance operates two cases against the deployed service. For an interrupted settled purchase, the operator retains the original dispatch, independently reconciles its native transfer and continues unfinished receiving under that same purchase. Completion requires the full selected result in the customer application and a record that delivery recovery caused no additional payment. An uncertain signed outcome remains attached to its original intent until reconciliation establishes the financial result.

For a merchant-delivery failure, the original incident identifies the affected purchase, unfinished output or fulfillment step and named responder. The responder acknowledges the displayed incident revision, performs the permitted correction and continues the same delivery. Acceptance compares the whole recovered output with the agreed source, coverage and hashes, retains the actual fulfillment result and records the receiving engineer’s acknowledgment.

Both cases retain the original notification and acknowledgment, separate financial and delivery states, response and recovery clocks, residual findings and the receiving engineer’s same-case reopening after drain/restart. Monitoring coverage gaps remain visible. Observed recovery times and customer acceptance are recorded against the selected installation; they do not create an unmeasured service-level promise.

The funded purchase targets are ten in total across the two independent buyers during T2’s seven-day window and thirty in total across the two buyers during T3’s fourteen-day window. A completed purchase joins a distinct approved payment intent, an independently observed native transfer and its complete purchased output. Transactions count once within their network.

The full PR383 source and original answer baseline remain retained."},{"id":"architecture","text":"The system has six components: the merchant’s private source/release workspace; its public HTTP or MCP operation; the native Stellar SDK and facilitator; the buyer’s private approval and spending state; complete-result and delivery records; and merchant fulfillment/accounting. Node.js supplies merchant and buyer interfaces. Source adapters and receiving applications retain their own native data and operating semantics.

|Stage|Implemented behavior|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|Review and publish|The merchant selects a source edition or named live query, request schema, output, limits and resolved payment options. Review includes source rights, route, network, asset, recipient, amount and authorization lifetime. Source or terms changes become later reviewed states.|
|Connect the source|Adapters preserve types, missing and null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select authorized access. The output identifies its source edition.|
|Approve and purchase|The buyer retains the endpoint, method or MCP tool, arguments, selected terms and scope. The remote schema and challenge must match before signing. Per-payment limits and the application’s existing reservation/budget owner govern spending.|
|Settle and deliver|The facilitator verifies and settles the native authorization. The application retains the server outcome, complete output and durable merchant notification. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the transaction’s network, asset, parties and atomic amount.|
|Use and continue|The receiving application opens all pages and files required by the task. A parent acquisition retains its priced requests and unfinished coverage. Earlier acquired output remains available when a later source edition changes.|
|Operate and hand over|The customer selects its release, HTTPS service, restricted administration and supervision. A receiving engineer can drain, restart, roll back and restore the installation with its operating history and complete customer files.|


**Recurring editorial data products.** The delivered WordPress merchant workspace turns a later source edition into a reviewable customer product. The operator saves an approved baseline as a refresh plan, continues the original native capture, inspects the complete source and projected changes, and approves the exact candidate before issuing its successor through the existing publisher. The same browser, CLI and agent interfaces preserve earlier acquired editions, original request identities and unfinished decisions when another engineer receives the workspace. This supplies a concrete recurring-use workflow for the selected customer installations. [Merged implementation and complete operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/1135e64cca2da5948c2d3e2c78119094d88f41d2/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/wordpress/REFRESH.md).

For paid MCP, the HTTP endpoint, tool and arguments are retained separately from the payment resource. An unsigned call obtains the challenge. Its full payment option, including authorization timeout, must match the saved quote before the buyer retains dispatch state and sends the signed call. The official MCP SDK carries payment and settlement metadata. HTTP operations use the native HTTP transport.

Each installation retains a compatibility profile identifying its complete source release, installed buyer and signer SDK versions, facilitator registration, network, supported asset, authorization flow and fee policy. The original approval and signer checks must accept that profile before dispatch. A provider or network change receives an explicit new selection and preserves earlier purchases and source editions. T2 receives the same useful service through both testnet facilitators; T3 receives both mainnet merchant installations under their actual selected profiles.

Recovery keeps server confirmation, independently observed transfer, complete output, receiver acknowledgment and fulfillment separately visible. An uncertain signed response stays attached to its original dispatch for reconciliation. Reopening an acquired result uses saved work; unfinished delivery continues from its original intent. A changed request or new purchase receives a new review.

Browser, terminal, typed clients and MCP operate the same retained workspaces. Customer exports include configuration selection, history and all referenced files. The receiving host supplies current authorized secret references. Buyer accounting also carries reviewed expense and credit allocations into connected QuickBooks and Xero accounts, with review of changed charts, affected mappings and journal lines before application.

The merchant's pricing workspace connects those operations to its customer offer. It retains the approved tariff and saved uniform quote, selects the actual usage period and counting basis, and compares their values with the recorded supplier-cost basis. The operator enters the monthly quantity for a proposed change, reviews the resulting native price, and carries the measured source into an ordinary customer quotation revision. The original pricing, scenario and Commercial workspaces retain the same requests and history. [Merged usage, pricing and quotation workflow](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/318).

The merchant financial workspace carries that paid operation into its original settlement accounting and customer records. An invoice can issue reviewed Stellar wallet terms; native receiving verifies the returned transfer and applies its original customer receipt. Issued service invoices retain exact amounts and billing identity; actual receipts, dated allocations and credits determine the balance. Reviewed installment plans distribute that balance across due dates and preserve every customer edition. The Xero handover maps issued invoices and credits to the receiving organisation's original templates, retains returned document IDs and exact amounts, and continues corrections through the same package family. Native network, asset and atomic amount remain attached to the original settlement; commercial valuations retain their explicit basis. Acceptance operates two cases against the deployed service. For an interrupted settled purchase, the operator retains the original dispatch, independently reconciles its native transfer and continues unfinished receiving under that same purchase. Completion requires the full selected result in the customer application and a record that delivery recovery caused no additional payment. For a merchant-delivery failure, the original incident identifies the affected purchase, unfinished output or fulfillment step and named responder. Both cases retain the original notification and acknowledgment, separate financial and delivery states, response and recovery clocks, residual findings and the receiving engineer’s same-case reopening after drain/restart. Monitoring coverage gaps remain visible. Observed recovery times and customer acceptance are recorded against the selected installation; they do not create an unmeasured service-level promise.

The funded purchase targets are ten in total across the two independent buyers during T2’s seven-day window and thirty in total across the two buyers during T3’s fourteen-day window. The cohort counts distinct accountable operator IDs whose reviewed deployment identifies an independent operator or customer, its buyer or merchant role, source basis, required network and operating or handed-over state. The buyer retains signing and aggregate spending authority; the merchant controls its resource and terms.

We compose the existing x402 Exact Stellar scheme, SDKs, token contracts and facilitators, including the selected provider’s actual payment requirements and optional discovery extension. The existing MPP Charge integration retains its own challenge and recovery model.

There are close alternatives. [ApiCharge](https://communityfund.stellar.org/project/apicharge-djv) combines service publication and consumption with Soroban settlement and signed agreements. [Nirium](https://github.com/nirium-protocol/nirium) provides Stellar payment SDKs, seller middleware, MCP and CLI interfaces. [MPP Router](https://www.mpprouter.dev/how-it-works) supplies service discovery and paid calls; [Stellar Raven](https://raven.stellar.org/docs) supplies ecosystem context and integration operations through MCP. Our application completes the customer’s continuing operation around payment: source review, complete paginated or file output, receiving into its business application, interrupted-operation recovery, and transfer of the working service to another maintainer.

We propose [Open Track](https://stellar.gitbook.io/scf-handbook/scf-awards/build-award/open-track) for this reusable merchant-and-buyer operating application. The full PR383 source and original answer baseline remain retained."},{"id":"architecture","text":"The architecture has six components: a private merchant source/release workspace; its public HTTP or MCP operation; the Stellar SDK and facilitator; private buyer approval and spending state; retained delivery records and complete output; and merchant fulfillment/accounting.

1. **Select and publish.** The merchant chooses an authorized source edition or named live query, schema, output and limits. Review resolves the route, network, asset, recipient, amount and authorization lifetime. Later source or terms changes become separately reviewed states.
2. **Connect the source.** Adapters preserve types, null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select access. The returned result identifies its source edition.
3. **Approve and pay.** The buyer retains the HTTP method or MCP tool, arguments, scope and payment option. The remote schema and full challenge, including authorization lifetime, must match before signing. For paid MCP, the endpoint, tool and arguments remain separate from the payment resource; the official MCP SDK carries payment and settlement metadata. Per-payment limits and the existing reservation/budget owner govern aggregate spending.
4. **Settle and receive.** The facilitator verifies and settles the native authorization. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the network, asset, parties and atomic amount. The application retains the complete output, merchant notification and receiving acknowledgment. A multi-request acquisition keeps its aggregate cost and unfinished coverage. Saved prepaid calls retain their selected pass; a replacement links to its predecessor and acquired results remain available.
5. **Use and account.** The receiving application opens every page and file needed for the task. Merchant pricing connects the selected tariff and saved uniform quote to an actual usage period, counting basis and supplier-cost basis. A reviewed price change carries its measured source into the customer quotation and original invoice or service records.
6. **Recover and hand over.** Server confirmation, observed transfer, output and fulfillment retain separate states. An uncertain signed response is reconciled through its original dispatch. The receiving engineer restores configuration, history and customer files, supplies authorized secret references and continues the same operation.

Node.js supplies the merchant, buyer, browser, CLI, typed-client and MCP interfaces. Source adapters and receiving applications retain their native semantics. The maintained implementation also uses Python and SQLite for typed data and saved queries, and PHP for WordPress/WooCommerce integration. Representative completed operations demonstrate the common customer workflow:

|Operation|Completed outcome|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|Municipal data|A Queens HPD selection received all 144 rows in paid pages of 100 and 44. Both 10,000-stroop transfers finalized, and the complete CSV/JSONL edition reopened with its source and accounting.|
|Paid agent query|One 50,000-stroop purchase returned 100 MariaDB rows, 14 columns and 53,468 bytes. The purchase reopened with signing disconnected; the complete result reopened in another directory.|
|Filing analysis|A 10,000-stroop purchase delivered the 2024–2025 Genpact comparison: four disclosure pairs, five findings and all 1,027,807 bytes. The editable analyst workspace and a restored installation reopened the same comparison.|
|Air-quality reporting|One public-archive request retained all 140 observations across six sensor series for Del Norte’s May 3, 2022 local day. The reviewed HTML/JSON report reached a separate seven-file customer project and reopened without another source call.|
|Pipeline operations|The OpenLineage service-level workspace completed report export, editable receiving, cold reopening and replay of thirteen original requests. The receiving workspace retained revision 13 and the identical 66-file application export.|


A paid API operation acquired an eight-unit plan for 10,000 stroops and completed a saved four-value analysis. The execution consumed two units; its original request reopened with six available. Ten merchant and eight subsequent agent stages retained the order, full result, allowance and settlement outbox. An encrypted backup continued from 4,096 bytes to all 144,771 bytes after shutdown and reopened offline. A separate local portfolio operation preserved the selected pass across default changes, replacement and archiving, with no extra allowance on replay; its eighteen exercised operations add usage/recovery experience to the network-purchase baseline.

The original merchant accounting exercise completed invoice issue, credit, receipt allocation, Xero-format receiving, correction and cold reopening. The tariff example completed selection, native repricing, backup and receiving: a 1,250-request graduated tariff totaled $14.25 and produced the saved $0.0114 uniform quote.

The installed product also delivers named reports, spreadsheets and supporting files through Jobs and Resource library, retaining the original request, payment and completed attempt. Its Federal awards report preserves the source observations, every transaction page, exact monetary values and editable HTML/JSON/CSV analysis. The OpenLineage Quality extension adds dataset rules, saved evaluations and reasoned findings to the same operating workspace. These are source and receiving foundations for the selected customer adaptations.

The [current merged product](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/386) connects recorded usage to a reviewed price and customer quote, and includes the original billing, service agreement, payment plan and customer-closing operators in both merchant installation selections. Its customer continuation has produced the revised quotation and recipient work; the existing operator is continuing the joined interface and financial operation from that saved state.

The complete release also underwent an operator edit, recovered export and separate offline receiving, retaining all 2,411 entries and 2,115 unique objects. The merchant receiving operation completed twelve phases of source/result reads, interruption recovery, file delivery and cold receiving with zero additional payments.

A confirmed integrity contradiction opens an incident. Age, rate and capacity thresholds use the installation’s reviewed values.

Acceptance operates two cases against the deployed service. The full PR383 source and original answer baseline remain retained."},{"id":"architecture","text":"The architecture has six components: a private merchant source/release workspace; its public HTTP or MCP operation; the Stellar SDK and facilitator; private buyer approval and spending state; retained delivery records and complete output; and merchant fulfillment/accounting.

1. **Select and publish.** The merchant chooses an authorized source edition or named live query, schema, output and limits. Review resolves the route, network, asset, recipient, amount and authorization lifetime. Later source or terms changes become separately reviewed states.
2. **Connect the source.** Adapters preserve types, null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select access. The returned result identifies its source edition.
3. **Approve and pay.** The buyer retains the HTTP method or MCP tool, arguments, scope and payment option. The remote schema and full challenge, including authorization lifetime, must match before signing. For paid MCP, the endpoint, tool and arguments remain separate from the payment resource; the official MCP SDK carries payment and settlement metadata. Per-payment limits and the existing reservation/budget owner govern aggregate spending.
4. **Settle and receive.** The facilitator verifies and settles the native authorization. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the network, asset, parties and atomic amount. The application retains the complete output, merchant notification and receiving acknowledgment. A multi-request acquisition keeps its aggregate cost and unfinished coverage. Saved prepaid calls retain their selected pass; a replacement links to its predecessor and acquired results remain available.
5. **Use and account.** The receiving application opens every page and file needed for the task. Merchant pricing connects the selected tariff and saved uniform quote to an actual usage period, counting basis and supplier-cost basis. A reviewed price change carries its measured source into the customer quotation and original invoice or service records.
6. **Recover and hand over.** Server confirmation, observed transfer, output and fulfillment retain separate states. An uncertain signed response is reconciled through its original dispatch. The receiving engineer restores configuration, history and customer files, supplies authorized secret references and continues the same operation.

Node.js supplies the merchant, buyer, browser, CLI, typed-client and MCP interfaces. Source adapters and receiving applications retain their native semantics. The maintained implementation also uses Python and SQLite for typed data and saved queries, and PHP for WordPress/WooCommerce integration. 2. **Connect the source.** Adapters preserve types, null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select access. The returned result identifies its source edition.
3. **Approve and pay.** The buyer retains the HTTP method or MCP tool, arguments, scope and payment option. The remote schema and full challenge, including authorization lifetime, must match before signing. For paid MCP, the endpoint, tool and arguments remain separate from the payment resource; the official MCP SDK carries payment and settlement metadata. Per-payment limits and the existing reservation/budget owner govern aggregate spending.
4. **Settle and receive.** The facilitator verifies and settles the native authorization. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the network, asset, parties and atomic amount. The application retains the complete output, merchant notification and receiving acknowledgment. A multi-request acquisition keeps its aggregate cost and unfinished coverage. Saved prepaid calls retain their selected pass; a replacement links to its predecessor and acquired results remain available.
5. **Use and account.** The receiving application opens every page and file needed for the task. Merchant pricing connects the selected tariff and saved uniform quote to an actual usage period, counting basis and supplier-cost basis. A reviewed price change carries its measured source into the customer quotation and original invoice or service records.
6. **Recover and hand over.** Server confirmation, observed transfer, output and fulfillment retain separate states. An uncertain signed response is reconciled through its original dispatch. The receiving engineer restores configuration, history and customer files, supplies authorized secret references and continues the same operation.

Node.js supplies the merchant, buyer, browser, CLI, typed-client and MCP interfaces. Source adapters and receiving applications retain their native semantics. The maintained implementation also uses Python and SQLite for typed data and saved queries, and PHP for WordPress/WooCommerce integration. input.title: purchase task allowance and current operator definitions
input.quote:
A completed purchase joins a distinct approved intent, an independently observed native transfer and complete useful output. Native transactions are counted once within each network. The cohort counts distinct accountable operator IDs whose reviewed deployment identifies an independent operator or customer, its buyer or merchant role, source basis, required network and operating or handed-over state. An operator’s agents and wallets share that identity; they do not create additional independent buyers. These are source-supported operator declarations, not automatic verification of corporate independence. Team-operated development purchases do not qualify. A returning buyer completes distinct intent groups on at least two UTC days. Reopening an acquired result or resuming its download continues the original purchase. Facilitators are also deduplicated by accountable operator for the same useful operation. [Original cohort operator guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/fcea2b04a19d9c14bbd337124ecdc83f5e36425c/stellar/scf_2026/sf47_budget_model/workspace/OPERATIONS-COHORT.md).

Cohort reporting includes completed/attempted purchases, complete/started parent datasets or files, returning buyers, accepted handovers and partial, unresolved, canceled and refunded outcomes. Required fulfillment remains separately visible. This makes the funded targets assessable against the whole observation window.
